title: What are the AWS load balancer types (ALB, NLB, Gateway LB), and when do you choose ALB (L7, HTTP routing, path/host rules) vs NLB (L4, ultra-low latency, static IP, TCP/UDP)?
shortTitle: AWS Load Balancer Types and Choosing ALB vs NLB
keyPoints: ALB operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and routes by path, host header, method, query string, and headers.
NLB operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS) with ultra-low latency, static IPs per AZ, and millions of connections per second.
Gateway LB operates at Layer 3/4 and inserts third-party appliances like firewalls transparently into the traffic path.
ALB is the default for microservices because it does path-based routing, TLS termination, and HTTP-level health checks.
NLB is chosen when traffic is non-HTTP, a partner needs a fixed IP to whitelist, or the workload needs the lowest possible latency.
An NLB in front of an ALB combines static IPs with Layer 7 routing when both are needed.

s1_definition.oneliner: ALB reads the request and routes by content at Layer 7, NLB just forwards packets blazingly fast at Layer 4, and GWLB inserts security appliances in the path.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **ALB (Application Load Balancer)** – operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS); reads the request path, host header, and cookies to route traffic with path-based and host-based rules; supports TLS termination, sticky sessions, HTTP/2, and WebSockets.
- **NLB (Network Load Balancer)** – operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS); forwards packets with ultra-low latency, gives a static IP per Availability Zone, preserves the client source IP, and handles millions of connections per second.
- **GWLB (Gateway Load Balancer)** – operates at Layer 3/4 using the GENEVE protocol; transparently inserts third-party virtual appliances like firewalls and intrusion-detection systems into the traffic path.
- **Target group** – the set of backend targets (EC2, ECS, Lambda, IP addresses) that a load balancer routes to.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine the main branch of National Bank of India. The ALB is a smart receptionist who reads each form and sends loan forms to the loan desk and card complaints to the card desk based on what is written on them. The NLB is a very fast turnstile that just counts people and pushes them through to the next free counter without reading anything, so it is extremely quick. The GWLB is the security scanner at the entrance that every person must pass through before reaching any counter.

sections.s6_takeaway:
AWS Elastic Load Balancing gives three load balancer types, and I choose between them by the layer of the network I need to work at. The Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7, the HTTP layer, so it reads the request path, host header, cookies, and methods, which lets me route by content. This is my default for microservices, because behind one HTTPS listener I can send one path to the transfer service and another to the statement service, do TLS termination, run HTTP-level health checks, and support HTTP/2 and WebSockets.

The Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4, the TCP and UDP layer. It does not read application data; it just forwards packets, which makes it extremely fast and able to handle millions of connections per second with very low latency. I reach for it when the traffic is not HTTP, when I need a static IP that a partner can whitelist in their firewall, or when I must preserve the client source IP end to end.

The Gateway Load Balancer is a specialist that inserts third-party network appliances like firewalls transparently into the traffic path using the GENEVE protocol, so all traffic can be inspected before reaching the application without the application knowing.

At National Bank of India I used an ALB in front of customer-facing microservices because I needed path-based routing and TLS termination, and an NLB in front of a raw TCP settlement feed because the partner bank's firewall team would only allow a single fixed IP address. A senior point I always mention is that these are not mutually exclusive: when I need both a static IP and Layer 7 routing, I place an NLB in front of an ALB.

Remember one sentence: ALB routes by HTTP content at Layer 7 and is the default for microservices, NLB forwards packets ultra-fast at Layer 4 and gives static IPs, and GWLB inserts security appliances transparently.
